title: Introduce invocation-clock metrics and adaptive log-fidelity controller
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces invocation-phase timing metrics (enqueue/schedule/kv/kernel/emit), an adaptive log-fidelity controller that dynamically adjusts log sampling per-tenant based on cost and tail latency signals, new dashboard panels for token-clock cost attribution, and a safety throttle to prevent logging ingestion storms.
description:
Context and motivation:
We see recurring high cost and storage growth from high-fidelity logging during bursty or anomalous traffic. Existing sampling policies are static and do not reliably surface the small fraction of invocations that drive most token-level cost and tail latency. This PR adds a lightweight invocation-clock metric stream that breaks down per-invocation time into phases (enqueue, scheduling, KV lookup, kernel run, token_emit). Those phase timings are used by a new adaptive log-fidelity controller to raise fidelity for suspicious invocations (high kernel time, high token-cost, or unusual phase skew) and to reduce fidelity on stable, low-cost traffic, reducing overall log volume while improving signal-to-noise for incident investigations.

Summary of changes (single-line commits high-level):
- add services/invoke/clock_metrics.go: record phase timestamps, emit compact phase histogram and per-invocation cost tags
- add controllers/log_fidelity/controller.go: adaptive policy engine + tenant policy store + safety throttle
- add observability/dashboards/token_clock_cost_panel.json: dashboard panels for phase-level tail and cost attribution
- add observability/alerts/phase-slow-alerts.yaml: new alert rules (SLO-calibrated) for per-phase tail regressions
- add docs/observability/log-fidelity.md: operator guide and tuning knobs
- unit tests for controller policy logic and load tests for safety throttle
- small SDK change: redwood-sdk-python -> expose phase metadata in responses for opt-in debugging

Files changed (high level):
- services/invoke/clock_metrics.go (core instrumenting, ~250 LOC): emits compact proto with phase micros, token counts, model size & quant flags
- controllers/log_fidelity/controller.go (policy engine, ~420 LOC): supports rules: threshold, percentile-based triggers, running-window decay, cost-budget gating
- controllers/log_fidelity/policy_store.go: pluggable tenant policy store (in-memory + redis backend hooks)
- observability/dashboards/token_clock_cost_panel.json: new panels (phase waterfall, cost contribution table, phase skew heatmap)
- observability/alerts/phase-slow-alerts.yaml: alerts for 95/99 phase latency increases and for safety throttle activation
- docs/observability/log-fidelity.md: instructions, recommended policies, and rollback guidance
- sdk/python/redwood/response_meta.py: attach opt-in _phase_clock metadata to responses
- tests/controller_policy_test.go, tests/invoke_clock_integration_test.go: unit/e2e tests

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Clock encoding: we emit a compact int32 microsecond vector per-phase with a shared invocation id. This keeps payloads small and allows downstream rollups.
- Controller is conservative by default: default policy increases fidelity only after a 3-sample sustained signal or single high-cost invocation marked by kernel>500ms and cost>5 tokens-equivalent.
- Safety throttle: controller includes a global circuit-breaker: if log-ingest rate > 1.5x baseline for a tenant or total qps spike causes >20% CPU on the log pipeline, controller enters temporary backoff and switches to header-only sampling. This avoids cascading cost spikes.

Review conversation (high level, preserved chronology):
- Alex Nguyen (review): "Nice instrumentation. Two asks: 1) can we avoid adding a hot path allocation in services/invoke for the common fast-path? 2) policy_store needs a TTL eviction test."
- Maya (author): "Addressed: pool-allocated proto buffer and moved TTL eviction test into policy_store_test.go. PTAL."
- Priya Rao (review): "Controller logic looks solid. Suggest adding an explicit metric for 'fidelity_switch_count' so we can track controller churn."
- Maya: "Added fidelity_switch_count and documented expected bounds in docs. Also added an integration test to assert the throttle flips no more than once per 10s in the synthetic traffic scenario."
- Liam O'Connor (SRE): "Alert tuning: 95->99 thresholds look noisy in canary; reduced sensitivity and added a rolling baseline compare (last 30m vs prior 6h). Also requested a dashboard panel showing budget burn rate."
- Maya: "Adjusted alerts and added budget burn-rate panel. CI flake: tests/invoke_clock_integration_test.go failed intermittently due to timing in CI; added deterministic clock stub in tests to stabilize."
- Approvals: Alex, Priya, Liam approved after fixes.

CI and rollout details:
- CI: build, unit tests, integration tests (invocation simulation), linters. Initial CI run: one flaky integration failure; rerun green. Final CI status: pass.
- Canary rollout: controller rolled out to canary cluster for 48h with tenant opt-in flag enabled. Observed 34% reduction in high-fidelity log volume for non-anomalous tenants and zero safety-throttle incidents. Two tenants opted into higher fidelity and provided immediate SRE-relevant traces that tracked down an upstream kernel contention bug.

Operational runbook and rollback:
- docs/observability/log-fidelity.md contains runbook: how to disable controller (feature flag), how to adjust per-tenant policy, how to read fidelity_switch_count and throttle events.
- Rollback action: disable feature flag and flush in-memory policy cache; policy_store persisted configs are unaffected.

Why this is different from existing work:
- We instrument per-invocation phase timings (clock) rather than coarse per-stage histograms, enabling precise attribution of token cost to specific runtime phases and better targeting of log fidelity increases where they matter. The adaptive controller ties telemetry to operational cost, not just latency alone.

Testing and benchmarks:
- Unit coverage: controller policy branching ~85% coverage.
- Load bench: synthetic 10k rps mix, observed controller CPU overhead <2% on control plane and log-ingest reduction of 28-40% depending on policy aggressiveness.

Merge outcome:
- PR merged via squash on 2026-02-18 after approvals and green CI. A follow-up PR will add an RBAC entry for tenant policy editing UI in the console (tracked ENG-410).

Notes for follow-ups:
- Expose phase-level histograms to the metrics-aggregation tier for low-cost rollups (ENG-401).
- Investigate ML-based anomaly policy to replace heuristic thresholds (ENG-402).
